verses.text: God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth.

The fear of you and the dread of you will be on every animal of the earth, and on every bird of the sky. Everything that moves along the ground, and all the fish of the sea, are delivered into your hand.
Every moving thing that lives will be food for you. As I gave you the green herb, I have given everything to you.
But flesh with its life, that is, its blood, you shall not eat.
I will surely require your blood of your lives; at the hand of every animal I will require it. At the hand of man, even at the hand of every man’s brother, I will require the life of man.
Whoever sheds man’s blood, his blood will be shed by man, for God made man in his own image.
Be fruitful and multiply. Increase abundantly in the earth, and multiply in it.”
God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying,
“As for me, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your offspring after you,
and with every living creature that is with you: the birds, the livestock, and every animal of the earth with you, of all that go out of the ship, even every animal of the earth.
I will establish my covenant with you: All flesh will not be cut off any more by the waters of the flood. There will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”
God said, “This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.
When I bring a cloud over the earth, that the rainbow will be seen in the cloud,
and I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the waters will no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
The rainbow will be in the cloud. I will look at it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”
God said to Noah, “This is the token of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is on the earth.”
The sons of Noah who went out from the ship were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham is the father of Canaan.
These three were the sons of Noah, and from these, the whole earth was populated.
Noah began to be a farmer, and planted a vineyard.
He drank of the wine and got drunk. He was uncovered within his tent.
Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside.

Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it on both their shoulders, went in backwards, and covered the nakedness of their father. Their faces were backwards, and they didn’t see their father’s nakedness.
Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done to him.
He said, “Canaan is cursed. He will be a servant of servants to his brothers.”
He said, “Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Shem. Let Canaan be his servant.
May God enlarge Japheth. Let him dwell in the tents of Shem. Let Canaan be his servant.”
Noah lived three hundred fifty years after the flood.
All the days of Noah were nine hundred fifty years, and then he died.

footnotes.content: After the judgment of the flood, the same blessing God spoke over Adam falls again on Noah and his sons. I take heart that when the waters recede, our God is still a God who blesses, and that all true blessing ultimately flows from Him who will one day make all things new in Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A new order is established: the fear of man now rests on the creatures. This is not cruelty, but a merciful restraint after such devastation, reminding me that even in a broken world, God still sets boundaries to preserve life until His purposes are complete.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God broadens what He gives for food, showing His care for those who remain. Yet every gift comes from His hand, and I am learning to receive even the simplest provision with gratitude, for all good things find their source in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God draws a clear line: life belongs to Him. The blood, the seat of life, is not to be treated carelessly. I see here a tenderness that points me to the greater truth that our lives, and the life of our Savior poured out for us, are precious beyond measure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord Himself takes up the cause for human life. He requires an accounting, not out of vengeance alone, but because life is His to guard. That gives weight to every life, and it makes me all the more thankful that Jesus bore the full account for sinners like me.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here is the reason for it all: man is made in God's own image. I cannot forget that this is not a small thing. If our image-bearing is so precious that murder demands judgment, how much more precious are we that the One who bears God's image perfectly, Jesus Christ, willingly laid down His life to redeem us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again the charge to be fruitful and multiply. After judgment, God still calls for life to go on. I find it sweet that even in a world marked by loss, the God of resurrection keeps giving the gift of new life and calls His people to trust Him for it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God speaks personally to Noah and his sons as a family. I am reminded that the God who judges the world also speaks tenderly to those He has spared, drawing them into His covenant and caring for generations yet to come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Behold, the Lord says: 'I establish my covenant.' It is His initiative from first to last. How like our God to bind Himself in faithfulness when we could never bind ourselves to Him. That is the very heart of the covenant love we have in Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This covenant reaches farther than I might think - to every living creature with them. Our God is not just concerned with saving people, but He cares for all He has made. One day, in Christ, the whole creation will groan no more and be set free.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God puts His own faithfulness on display: never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all flesh. I lean on that promise when the world feels unstable. For those in Christ, we have an even surer promise - God will never again turn His face away in judgment from those covered by His Son.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord delights to give a token of His covenant. He knows our weakness and gives us something to look at when our hearts forget. How gracious of Him to stoop to reassure us with visible reminders of His unshakeable faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God sets His rainbow in the cloud - a bow of promise hung between heaven and earth. Long ago, I wonder if weary Noah looked up and trembled with gratitude. Now, when I see it, I look beyond the bow to Jesus, our true peace, who has turned away the storm of God's wrath for all who belong to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the clouds, which once brought terror, will now be the canvas for mercy. Our God redeems the very things that used to frighten us. What a comfort to know that His faithfulness meets us even in the dark clouds of this life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God says, 'I will remember my covenant.' It is not that He forgets, but that He acts in faithfulness for His own name's sake. What rest for my soul - my hope does not hang on my memory of God, but on God's faithful memory of His covenant mercy to me in Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The rainbow is in the cloud, and God says He will look at it and remember. I love this - the Lord delights to gaze upon the sign of His own mercy. So I may look up and rest: He looks upon that bow, and He looks upon His people in Jesus with steadfast, covenant love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God repeats the token to Noah once more, sealing it with His word. After all he had seen, Noah needed that reassurance, and so do I. The God who spoke it still speaks faithfulness over all who trust in the greater covenant secured by Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three sons go forth from the ark to repopulate the earth. I think of the weight of it - the whole human race will come from these three. And yet from one of their lines would come Abraham, and from Abraham, our Lord Jesus, the true Seed through whom all nations will be blessed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Noah's three sons came all the peoples of the earth. I am struck by God's purpose - He meant for humanity to fill the earth again with worshippers. One day, by grace, a vast multitude from every tribe and tongue will worship the Lamb together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah, the righteous preacher of righteousness, now begins as a farmer. How humbling - even the men God uses most mightily are still ordinary men. After the greatest deliverance, life returns to planting and tending, a reminder that grace meets us in the everyday, not just the mountaintop.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Oh, how quickly we fall. The man who walked with God is overcome by wine and uncovered in his tent. It warns this old heart: no matter how far God has brought us, we still need a Savior. Our hope is never in our own righteousness, but only in Jesus, our righteous covering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ham sees his father's shame and delights to make it known. There is a world of difference between sorrow over sin and scorn toward a brother's weakness. I pray the Lord keeps me from gloating over another's fall, and instead clothes others with the mercy He has so freely clothed me with.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blessed are the sons who walk backwards in love. Shem and Japheth cover their father without looking on his shame, showing reverence and tender care. This is the way of Christ - He came not to expose our naked shame to scorn, but to cover us with His own robes of righteousness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah awakens and knows what his youngest son has done. Sin always finds us out, though not always in the moment we commit it. Yet for those who belong to Jesus, our sins are fully known to God, and fully covered by the blood of our great High Priest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A sobering word falls from Noah's lips under the weight of grief and conviction. We see the seriousness of dishonoring those God has placed over us. Still, I rest in this: God's ultimate plan of redemption will not be thwarted by human sin - He will bring blessing through the line of Shem to all families of the earth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah blesses Shem and points to Yahweh, the God of Shem. I love that the true blessing is knowing the Lord Himself. From Shem's line would come the God-Man, Jesus, through whom every believer can say with joy, 'Yahweh is my God, and I am His forever.'
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Looking back from a longer road, readers today hear an echo of God's mercy: He enlarges and brings many into the tents of Shem, that is, into fellowship with the God of Shem. As of 2026-10, I rejoice that by grace, people from every nation now dwell in the family of God through faith in Jesus, the true Son of Abraham.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah lives long after the flood, watching a new world grow from the remnant God preserved. It reminds me that after God's judgment comes the gift of years to walk in gratitude. May my latter days be marked less by strength, and more by thankful trust in my faithful Savior.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Noah died at 950 years, full of days, yet he was still a sinner in need of a greater righteousness. That makes me long all the more for the day when God's people die in faith and enter the true rest - not the rest after flood, but the rest of being forever at home with Jesus, our Ark and our righteousness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
